issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
covered_actors: organizations of all sizes, public or private, in any sector

evidence.quote: intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment
foster the development of innovative approaches to address characteristics of trustworthiness including ... accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable
Framework users and AI actors should consider and encompass trustworthiness characteristics during pre-design, design and development, deployment, use, and test and evaluation
NIST has produced the AI RMF as a voluntary Framework
evidence.source_section: Will private or public sector organizations be required to use the Framework?

evidence.quote: Organizations seeking specific guidance for how to achieve AI RMF function outcomes may borrow as many – or as few – suggestions as apply to their industry use case or interests

implementation_notes: The AI RMF is explicitly voluntary; Congress directed NIST to develop it as such. A companion Playbook provides actionable suggestions. No penalties or enforcement mechanisms are specified.
